title: Points, lines, line segments and rays

accuracy.evidence: Checked on 24 Nov 2026 against CCSS 4.G.A.1 (draw and identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles and perpendicular and parallel lines) and CCSS 4.MD.C.5a (an angle is formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint), and the NCETM primary geometry glossary: a line has no endpoints and infinite length, a segment has two endpoints and a fixed length, a ray has one endpoint and is named endpoint first. The lab's lengths are true to the grid: figure 1 is 4 squares, figure 2 is a 3-4-5 diagonal (5), figure 3 runs from 1.5 to 6.5 (5). Angle classes match NC Year 4 (acute under 90, obtuse between 90 and 180). The house has exactly 6 segments and 5 vertices.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented Grade 4 geometry slips: calling every straight mark a line (step 1 makes all three from the same two points), measuring a ray (step 2 prediction and the refusal messages for figures 4 to 6), ray AB = ray BA (step 3 prediction and the 'starts at' and 'goes towards' refusals), arrows as pointers (challenge 'arrow' slip), longer arms meaning a bigger angle (Longer arms button and 'arms' slip), and counting a shared side twice (house refuses BC twice with the shared-side reason).

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanisms are about this topic's own objects: draggable grid points joined as segment, ray or line with endpoint dots and arrowheads drawn from board-edge clipping; a ruler that only measures figures with two endpoints; ray building by tapping the endpoint then a through-point on three collinear points, which also shows ray RQ and ray RP are the same ray; an angle from two rays at a vertex with arm length switchable; and segment hunting in a house. The gate measured under 30% source overlap with every other flag_*.js.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners discover each rule by acting before the strip confirms it: choosing Ray or Line visibly removes endpoints and adds arrows; tapping a ray to measure is refused with the reason, while segments give cm lengths; building ray QP from P is refused with 'must start at Q'; the angle readout changes as the arm turns but not when the arms lengthen; and the house count stops at 6 when BC is tapped again.

predictions.evidence: Two committed predictions with tempting wrong answers: 'Can you measure how long a ray is?' (tempting: yes, from the endpoint to the arrow), disproved when the ruler refuses figures 4 and 5; and 'Is ray QR the same ray as ray QP?' (tempting: yes, both start at Q), disproved when the two rays are drawn pointing opposite ways. The task cannot complete until a prediction is locked, and the done message names the prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Eight challenge questions; every wrong option carries a tagged slip with its own message: 'ends' counts endpoints 2, 1, 0; 'length' explains why a ray has no length; 'order' explains the endpoint-first rule; 'arrow' says the arrow means for ever; 'vertex' names the shared endpoint; 'arms' says size is the turn not the arm length; 'twice' says each side is one segment counted once.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and only the topic's own terms (point, endpoint, segment, ray, line, vertex, angle), each defined where it first appears; validate_lessons.py passed the kid and adult readability limits. Lab strips are one or two short sentences, and button labels are two or three words.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph teaches one fact (points and naming; endpoints and arrows; endpoint-first naming; angles and segments in shapes). Adult paragraphs give the standard, precise definitions, the mistakes and what the lab does; the content gate found no filler phrases and under 12% overlap with any other lesson.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in dark and light themes for every step after Show me: the 12 x 8 board fills the width, point letters and length tags stay readable at 12 to 15 px, the stacked rays QR, QP and RP are labelled and do not overlap, the angle readout sits clear of the arms, and the buttons wrap onto two rows with nothing clipped.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin (join as segment, ray or line; Move B; Measure 1 to 6; Point P, Q, R; Open and Close 15 degrees; Longer or Shorter arms; Side BC to AC). The canvas aria-label is updated with every message, the challenge feedback is a polite live region, and walk.cjs found axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.

sources: DfE National Curriculum in England: mathematics programmes of study, Year 3 and Year 4 geometry (2013)
NCETM, Primary mathematics glossary: line, line segment, ray, vertex
